title: Environment access and process termination utilities (CodeSaathi extension)
learningObjectives: Use getenv and handle the possibility that an environment variable is absent.
Explain why environment values are external input and why the returned string must not be modified or freed.
Distinguish the portable C environment interface from platform-specific mutation APIs.
Compare normal termination with exit, immediate termination with _Exit and abnormal termination with abort.
Explain atexit registration order and normal stream-flushing behaviour.
Choose safe configuration defaults and deliberate process exit statuses.

understand.concept: getenv retrieves an environment variable's value or returns a null pointer when unavailable. The standard library also provides exit, _Exit (since C99) and abort, which have different termination and cleanup behaviour. Environment values may be absent and must be treated as external input.
understand.whyItMatters: Environment variables influence configuration, paths and deployment. They are not guaranteed to exist or contain valid values. Choosing the wrong termination function can skip buffered output or registered cleanup handlers.
understand.analogy: A portable C interface is a contract between source code and the implementation.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy does not replace the exact C standard and implementation guarantees.

explain.narrative: Check getenv for NULL before using the result. Do not modify or free the returned string; it is managed by the implementation. Copy it into application-owned storage if it must be preserved independently. ISO C does not standardize setenv; identify platform-specific APIs explicitly. exit performs normal termination: atexit handlers run in reverse registration order and open streams are flushed and closed. Returning from the initial main call has the same normal-termination effect. _Exit terminates without the normal atexit and stream-flushing sequence. abort causes abnormal termination and may produce a diagnostic or core dump depending on the environment. Use EXIT_SUCCESS and EXIT_FAILURE for portable intent.

examples.title: Read optional configuration with a default
examples.explanation: getenv may return NULL when absent. This example also treats an empty value as a request for the default and never modifies or frees the returned string.

examples.title: Register a normal-termination handler
examples.explanation: atexit registers a no-argument, void-returning function. It runs during normal termination, including return from main or exit, but not in _Exit's immediate termination sequence or abort's abnormal termination.

practise.guidedTask: Run the configuration example with APP_MODE absent, empty and non-empty. Record which branch is selected.
practise.independentTask: Read an optional environment setting, validate it against an allow-list, use a safe default and register a normal-termination handler. Explain why getenv's pointer is not freed.
hints: Check bounds before accessing array elements.
Validate external text before conversion or use.
Use the matching standard-library interface and type.
Test normal, boundary and invalid-input cases.
Record implementation-specific assumptions instead of guessing.

questions.prompt: What may getenv return when a variable is unavailable?
options: An allocated empty string in every case.
A pointer the caller must free.
questions.explanation: The caller must check the result before using it as a string.

questions.prompt: What should a program do with the string returned by getenv?
options: Treat it as implementation-managed storage; do not modify or free it.
Write a null terminator into it.
questions.answer: Treat it as implementation-managed storage; do not modify or free it.
questions.explanation: The returned pointer is not an allocation transferred to the caller.

options: It performs normal termination processing including atexit handlers and stream flushing.
It skips all cleanup and flushes no streams.
questions.answer: It performs normal termination processing including atexit handlers and stream flushing.

questions.prompt: Which function terminates without normal atexit-handler processing and stream flushing?
questions.explanation: _Exit performs immediate termination without normal termination processing.

options: During normal termination, in reverse registration order.
questions.answer: During normal termination, in reverse registration order.
questions.explanation: Successfully registered handlers run in last-in, first-out order during normal termination.
